newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court denies abortion protester's appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court denies abortion protester's appeal.

text.p: The Supreme Court Monday rejected an appeal by a protester who claimed she should have had a jury trial for blocking access to an abortion clinic.
Marilyn Hatch and five other protesters were charged after a June 4, 1994 blockade in Milwaukee with violating a federal law guaranteeing access to abortion clinics.

Hatch claimed she was constitutionally entitled to a jury at her trial on the criminal charge, which carries a maximum penalty of six months in jail and a $10,000 fine. But the Supreme Court rejected her appeal without comment or dissent, siding with the Justice Department and letting stand a lower court ruling that upheld her conviction.

The defendants were found guilty in November 1995 by a federal judge who ruled after upholding the constitutionality of the law and turning down a request for a trial by jury. The judge held that the right to a jury trial applied only to "serious" offences, not "petty" offences. A U.S. appeals court agreed, saying the Supreme Court had held that a maximum six-month prison term was not enough to trigger a jury trial.

Hatch was sentenced to 30 days in jail and a $500 fine. In her appeal, she also argued that the 1994 law violated constitutional free-speech guarantees and that Congress lacked the power to adopt the measure, but the high court refused to hear those arguments, as it has in a number of earlier cases.
